author: Keystone Today
title: Altoona union official pleads guilty to embezzlement and falsifying financial report
text:
Altoona union official pleads guilty to embezzlement and falsifying financial report
Nicole DeStefano, a resident of Altoona, Pennsylvania, pleaded guilty on Sep. 15 to charges of embezzlement and falsification of an annual financial report in federal court, according to United States Attorney Troy Rivetti.
DeStefano, 52, entered her plea before United States District Judge Stephanie L. Haines to one count each of embezzling labor union assets and falsifying an annual financial report filed by a labor union. She served as secretary-treasurer for the American Postal Workers Union Local 776 in Altoona from 2015 through 2022, responsible for maintaining financial records, preparing reports, and issuing payments on behalf of the local.
The court was advised that in September 2022 a member discovered abnormal disbursements on the union’s 2021 annual financial report. DeStefano had signed the document as both treasurer and president without providing notice or allowing members to examine records. The Blair Township Police Department began an investigation and obtained a search warrant for DeStefano’s bank records.
Records showed that between December 2019 and August 2022, DeStefano wrote approximately 42 unauthorized checks totaling $30,411.68 from union accounts to herself or “cash.” An audit identified another 43 unauthorized debit transactions totaling almost $20,000. For three consecutive years, she omitted these disbursements from required reports filed with the Secretary of Labor. In September 2022, she transferred $8,500 back into the union account before resigning her position.
Judge Haines scheduled sentencing for January 19, 2027. The law allows for up to five years in prison and fines up to $10 million or twice any pecuniary gain. Sentencing will be determined based on federal guidelines considering offense seriousness and criminal history. As a result of her felony conviction for embezzlement, DeStefano is barred from holding union office for thirteen years.
Assistant United States Attorney Brendan J. McKenna is prosecuting the case with investigations conducted by the Blair Township Police Department and U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Labor-Management Standards.
